assertions.source: b at q_0 two ways: √(q⁴+q²+1)/(q²+1) vs √((h²+3)/(h²+4)) with h = q − q⁻¹ — the two forms this function's docstring gives, written with no shared subexpression. u = b·ℏ_q² carries every ppb figure in this audit.

assertions.source: b(q_0⁻¹) vs b(q_0) — an evaluation at the BAR-CONJUGATE point, independent of the evaluation at q_0. This is the Lean-proved QOU.QBeta.hoefsmitBSq_bar_even (audit 2026-06-20-hoefsmit-b-bar-parity-correction.md); the bar-ODD (q−q⁻¹)/(q+q⁻¹) that once sat in `hoefsmit_b` flips sign here.

description: Q_β c_3 evaluation comparison: J_Hopf(q=1)=-2 vs J_Hopf(q_0)=-(q_0²+q_0⁻²) at canonical substrate. Reaffirms that Rule A (constant -2) is the only structurally legitimate c_3 since Taylor coefficients of a q-series MUST be q-anchor-independent. The 3.47% 'm_p-pin swing' in PR #1479's deep audit is the c_4 truncation error, NOT evidence that c_3 = -2 is wrong.

data.interpretation: Rule A (c_3 = J_Hopf(q=1) = -2) is q_0-INDEPENDENT — passes the Taylor-coefficient stability test required for a true Habiro coefficient. Rule B (c_3 = J_Hopf(q_0) = -2.044) is q_0-DEPENDENT — cannot be a Taylor coefficient (those are constants). The 3.47% 'swing' between A and B IS the c_4·u⁴ truncation error, BOUNDED per rule 2 of the canonical framing — NOT evidence c_3 is wrong. Per the framing's Rule 4, dashboard should report c_3 = -2 in the 'near-match' tier (still pending Habiro-element identification per the α_EM PR #1511 template).

audit_completed.meaning: the 50 dps Rule A vs Rule B comparison ran to its verdict

caveats: STALE COMMENT (recorded, not repaired): the c_4-estimate comment in section [5] states "b = hoefsmit_b(q) = (q-q⁻¹)/(q+q⁻¹)" — the bar-ODD form that `hoefsmit_b`'s own docstring says was REMOVED as wrong by ~8×. The code calls the corrected function; only the comment still describes the defect. The two b assertions above now fail if the code ever regresses to what the comment claims.

The 3.47% m_p-pin swing quoted in [3] and in the description is the audit's figure, not this run's: J(q_0)/J(q=1) − 1 computes to 2.18531% here. c_4 ≈ c_3·b⁴ is a natural-magnitude ESTIMATE with no independent route in this script (the empirical c_4 would have to come from the SDP extraction, whose c_k are now nulled as unresolved), so the truncation bound is recorded as data only.
